checks.label: The power or index shows how many times a number has been multiplied by itself: at every power on the first screen the row holds exactly that many tiles of the base, and its working multiplies that many copies
The base numbers are the same (9), so add the indices together (3 + 5 = 8): 9³ × 9⁵ = 9⁸, and the joined row holds 8 tiles of 9
Three of the eights from the top row and all of the eights on the bottom row have been crossed out, leaving eight multiplied by eight, eight squared
To raise to a power for a given base, multiply the indices: each grid holds its row of tiles once for every row, rows times tiles in a row
A second base is hatched and counted on its own: 2³ × 3² keeps three 2-tiles and two hatched 3-tiles, 8 × 9 = 72, not 6⁵ = 7776, and each bracket regroups into its own kinds of tile
Every line of working on every screen adds up at the number tried, and the first screen's working is right at every power from 1 to 6
Each puzzle draws the expression it asks about and accepts only its right answer, which equals the question at every number tried, while every wrong answer makes a different value
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer, and a wrong pick draws its own tiles to count beside the question's
Every demonstration has arrived within 5 s of its screen opening, nothing starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, and every change of power within 2.5 s
